description: Mock-interview transcripts with what a good debrief must and must not do. Scored by an LLM judge against the rubric plus hard checks (score band, mentions, no invented experience).

cases.resume: B.Sc. CS 2024. Projects: React/TypeScript dashboard (Next.js, MongoDB), Node REST API. Internship 3 months at a startup: React components, Jest tests.

transcript.content: What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect?

useEffect runs after the browser paints, so it doesn't block rendering; useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after DOM mutations but before paint, so you use it when you need to measure layout and avoid a flicker. In my dashboard I used useLayoutEffect once to measure a chart container before rendering the SVG, and useEffect for data fetching.
How would you avoid refetching the same data on every render?

Put the fetch in a useEffect keyed by the id, or better, use a cache layer like SWR or React Query which dedupes requests and gives stale-while-revalidate. In the internship we moved from manual useEffect fetches to SWR and the duplicate requests disappeared.
Tell me about a bug that took you a long time to find.

A stale closure: an interval callback read an old state value. I found it by logging renders, then fixed it with a ref holding the latest value, and wrote a Jest test with fake timers to lock it down.

cases.resume: Backend engineer, 4 years Node.js and Go, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Kafka. Owned the billing service at a fintech.

transcript.content: How do you make a payment operation idempotent?

Client sends an idempotency key; we store it with the result in Postgres with a unique constraint, so a retry returns the stored response instead of charging twice. We did exactly this for billing at my last job with a 24h TTL.
How would you design the Kafka consumers to handle a poison message?
Hmm, I think you just retry it? Maybe log it.
What happens to the rest of the partition while you retry?
I'm not sure, I haven't dealt with that.
